newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas scores gains despite late softening.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas scores gains despite late softening.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices rallied early Monday on prospects of a stronger NYMEX open but then faltered as futures began to retreat, market sources said.
Prices at the Henry Hub, La, on average were still up six cents from Friday to $2.23-2.26 per mmBtu, while Transco (Station 65) was quoted mostly in the high-$2.20s to about $2.30.
NYMEX's June Henry Hub gas futures slid to a low of $2.18, down 6.9 cents this morning, after a brief firmer opening to a high of $2.28.
Maintenance on Transco's Texas line will continue to cut about 400 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) out of a total capacity of about 600 mmcfd Tuesday through Thursday.
However, temperatures throughout most of the U.S., including Texas, are expected to hover below normal through this week, Weather Services Corp said.
South Texas prices gained an average of five cents to $2.10-2.15 as buyers balanced loads for the remainder of the month, traders said.
In the East, despite forecasts for cooler, rainy weather, New York city-gate prices rose more than five cents to the low-$2.50s.
Traders blamed the price uptick on the absence of some nuclear power due to unexpected outages.

The 1,100 megawatt (MW) Peach Bottom 2 nuclear unit in Pennsylvania was cut to about 74 percent power over the weekend for maintenance, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said. Also, the 610 MW Nine Mile Point 1 unit in New York was running at 25 percent power early Monday.
In response to the stronger Gulf market, Appalachian prices climbed three cents to about $2.40-2.45 on Columbia and CNG.
In the Midcontinent, prices rose four cents to an average range of $2.00-2.05, with late morning deals reported done below that range.
Permian gas sold mostly in the high-$1.90s to low-$2, up about five cents, despite much cooler weather in Texas and southern California.
At the Southern California border, prices also gained five cents to $2.18-2.20.
